chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from al-Rabi' ibn Yazid, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:
The upper hand is better than the lower hand, and begin with those whom you support.

key_terms.الْيَدُ السُّفْلَى: The lower hand — metaphor for the hand of the receiver, one who receives charity
key_terms.الْيَدُ الْعُلْيَا: The upper hand — metaphor for the hand of the giver, one who bestows charity
key_terms.تَعُولُ: Those whom you support/maintain — dependants, family members under one's financial care

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith 'the upper hand is better than the lower hand' mean in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) conveys two principles of Islamic charity ethics. First, it emphasizes the superior spiritual status of the giver over the receiver, echoing the well-known prophetic saying that 'the upper hand is better than the lower hand' — a teaching understood in early Muslim communities to mean that one who gives in charity is superior to one who receives it. Second, it establishes a priority order in giving: one must first fulfill the needs of one's own dependants (family) before extending charity to others.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Al Rabie who said, 
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying,
‘The higher (providing) hand is better than a lower (receiving) hand, and begin with the dependants’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman from Rabi’a ibn Yazid who has said the following: “I heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘
A providing hand is better than an asking hand, and you should begin providing for your family.’”
